title: Socketed spearhead
source_title: File:A complete cast iron spearhead, of probable Medieval date. (FindID 87221).jpg
creator: Birmingham Museums Trust, Caroline Johnson, 2005-02-10 15:48:53
credit: https://finds.org.uk/database/ajax/download/id/50970  Catalog:  https://finds.org.uk/database/images/image/id/50970/recordtype/artefacts    archive copy  at the    Wayback Machine     Artefact:  https://finds.org.uk/database/artefacts/record/id/87221
attribution: The Portable Antiquities Scheme/ The Trustees of the British Museum
source_description: A complete cast iron spearhead, of probable Medieval date (length: 120mm; width at blade: 20.4mm; thickness of blade: 8.4mm; diameter of end of shank: 17.3mm; weight: 56.95g).  The rounded wings of the blade are uneven to either side, with the rib clearly visible down the centre.  The shaft is hollow and in a one piece without a split to the side, like with Anglo Saxon types, indicating that this artefact is probably later.  There are possible remains of an iron rivet to the end of the shank, where the spearhead would have been fastened onto a wooden shaft.  The artefact is worn and in a corroded condition.
why: A narrow iron point and tubular socket give a simple spear a readable construction.
limitation: The source gives a broad probable medieval range, not a firm 1101 date. Rust and the modern measuring scale are not design details.
downloaded_image_changes: None; source rendition saved unchanged. Overview contains scaled copies.

title: Work dress and headcloth
source_title: File:Rekonstruert kvinnedrakt fra middelalderen ("kvinne med legende urter fra slaget på Stiklestad 1030") Hodelin skaut kjortel draktspenne forkle Medieval women's clothing Bergenhus festningsmuseum Fortress Military Museum Bergen A.jpg
creator: Wolfmann
source_description:
Reconstructed female dress (women's costume/clothing) with a simple  robe  (ankle-length  tunic ), an  apron  and a  headscarf  (veil) from the Norwegian  Viking Age  or Middle Ages, on display in the exhibition about women at war in the  Bergenhus Fortress Museum  (Norwegian:  Bergenhus festningsmuseum ) in  Bergen , Norway: 
    During the  Battle of Stiklestad  in 1030, a small house in the vicinity was used as an infirmary. The woman who did the work there cleaned wounds and applied healing herbs and bandages.    
  See  Early medieval European dress: Female dress  and  Women's clothing in 1100–1200 in European fashion .
evidence_type: Modern museum reconstruction presented as 1030 dress
why: Ankle-length work dress, head covering and apron provide options for Almodis and other adult villagers.
limitation: Reconstruction, not a surviving ensemble. Preserve Almodis’s covered hair and faded red-brown wool; an apron remains optional.
